messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Customers should also be able to email support and reply from their mail client. Add this with
Action Mailbox. Each business receives mail at its subdomain under `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN`,
default `support.example.test`; Acme gets `acme@support.example.test`.

Use Action Mailbox's relay ingress at `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails`, authenticated
with `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. In test, process incoming mail before the request completes
so a separate worker isn't needed.

Incoming mail should open a ticket with its subject and plain-text message.

Find the business from the recipients, including Cc. Ignore mail addressed to multiple businesses.
Reuse an existing customer, or create one and send a verification email so they can later use the portal.
Receiving email shouldn't verify their account.

When staff post a public reply to an email-origin ticket, email it to the requester. Give each
ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to
the right conversation. Only the requester may reply by email. Replies reopen pending or solved
tickets; a new message to the plain support address opens a new ticket.

Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry.
Ignore automated/list mail.

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(s) { s.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account

  scope :recently_active_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :matching_query, ->(query) {
    term = query.to_s.strip
    return all if term.blank?

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(term)}%"
    where(
      "tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern OR EXISTS (" \
      "SELECT 1 FROM comments " \
      "WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id " \
      "AND comments.public = TRUE " \
      "AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern" \
      ")",
      pattern: pattern
    )
  }

    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at

  end

    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      priority: priority,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      requester: {
        id: requester.id,
        name: requester.name,
        email: requester.email
      },
      assignee_id: assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee ? {
        id: assignee.id,
        name: assignee.name
      } : nil,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return if requester.nil? || account.nil?
    return if requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
  end

  def assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    if assignee.nil? || assignee.account_id != account_id || !assignee.staff? || assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    end
  end
end

    class RequestsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_account!
      before_action :require_session!
      before_action :require_active_account!

      def index
        scope = customer_requests.recently_active_first

        if params[:status].present?
          status_filter = params[:status].to_s
          unless Ticket::STATUSES.include?(status_filter)
            return render json: { error: "Invalid status filter" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
          scope = scope.where(status: status_filter)
        end

        result = paginate(scope)

        render json: result[:meta].merge(
          requests: result[:records].map(&:as_request_json)
        ), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        ticket = customer_requests.find(params[:id])
        render json: { request: ticket.as_request_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        request_attrs = params.require(:request)
        unless request_attrs.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          return render json: { error: "Invalid request payload" }, status: :bad_request
        end

        permitted = request_attrs.permit(:subject, comment: [ :body ])
        comment_attrs = permitted[:comment] || {}

        ticket = current_account.tickets.build(
          requester: current_user,
          subject: permitted[:subject],
          status: "open"
        )
        comment = ticket.comments.build(
          author: current_user,
          body: comment_attrs[:body],
          public: true
        )

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          ticket.save!
          comment.save!
        end

        render json: { request: ticket.reload.as_request_json }, status: :created
      end

      def update
        ticket = customer_requests.find(params[:id])
        request_attrs = params.require(:request)
        unless request_attrs.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          return render json: { error: "Invalid request payload" }, status: :bad_request
        end

        permitted = request_attrs.permit(:status, comment: [ :body ])

        has_comment = request_attrs.key?(:comment)
        has_status = permitted.key?(:status) && !permitted[:status].nil?

        unless has_comment || has_status
          return render json: { error: "Comment or status is required" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        if has_status && permitted[:status].to_s != "solved"
          if Ticket::STATUSES.include?(permitted[:status].to_s)
            return render json: { error: "Customers can only mark requests as solved" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          else
            return render json: { error: "Status is not included in the list" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
        end

        if has_comment && !request_attrs[:comment].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          return render json: { error: "Comment must be an object" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          if has_comment
            comment_body = permitted.dig(:comment, :body)
            ticket.comments.create!(
              author: current_user,
              body: comment_body,
              public: true
            )

            if has_status
              ticket.update!(status: "solved")
            elsif ticket.status.in?(%w[pending solved])
              ticket.update!(status: "open")
            end
          elsif has_status
            ticket.update!(status: "solved")
          end

module Api

    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      DEFAULT_PAGE = 1
      DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing, with: :render_parameter_missing

      private

      def require_account!
        subdomain = request.headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"].to_s.strip.downcase
        if subdomain.blank?
          return render json: { error: "X-Helpdesk-Account header is required" }, status: :bad_request
        end

        @current_account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomain)
        if @current_account.nil?
          render json: { error: "Account not found" }, status: :not_found
        end
      end

      def require_active_account!
        return if @current_account.nil?

        if @current_account.cancelled?
          render json: { error: "Account is cancelled" }, status: :forbidden
        end
      end

      def require_session!
        raw_token = extract_bearer_token
        @current_session = Session.authenticate_for_account(current_account, raw_token)
        if @current_session.nil?
          return render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
        end

        @current_user = @current_session.user
        if @current_user.suspended?
          render json: { error: "Unauthorized" }, status: :unauthorized
        end
      end

      def require_owner!
        return if current_user&.owner_of?(current_account)

        render json: { error: "Only the account owner can perform this action" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_admin!

        render json: { error: "Only admins can perform this action" }, status: :forbidden
      end

      def require_staff!
        return if current_user&.staff?

        render json: { error: "Only staff members can perform this action" }, status: :forbidden
      end

        page = parse_positive_int(params[:page], DEFAULT_PAGE)

        offset = (page - 1) * per_page
        records = scope.limit(per_page).offset(offset).to_a

          meta: {
            count: total_count,
            page: page,
            per_page: per_page,

            previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil

      def parse_positive_int(value, default)

        default

require "test_helper"

class RequestsAndTicketsTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  def create_and_verify_customer(subdomain:, name:, email:, password: "my-customer-password")
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
         params: { user: { name: name, email: email, password: password } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    token = extract_token_from_email(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/verify-email")[:token]

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
         params: { email_verification: { token: token } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
         as: :json
    assert_response :success
    json_response["user"]
  end

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)
    { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain, "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}" }
  end

  test "customer opens request, staff replies and updates status, customer replies reopen or solve" do
    create_and_verify_account(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test")
    acme = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme")
    agent = acme.users.create!(
      name: "Sam Agent",
      email: "agent@acme.test",
      password: "agent-password",
      role: "agent",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )

    avery = create_and_verify_customer(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test")
    avery_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password").dig("session", "token")
    owner_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password").dig("session", "token")
    agent_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "agent@acme.test", password: "agent-password").dig("session", ",
  "output_tail": "h "/api/v1/tickets/#{avery_ticket_id}",
          params: { ticket: { status: "archived" } },
          headers: auth_headers("acme", acme_owner_token),
          as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Cancelled account blocks requests & tickets, and purge deletes them cleanly
    post "/api/v1/account/cancel", headers: auth_headers("acme", acme_owner_token)
    assert_response :success

    new_owner_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password").dig("session", "token")
    get "/api/v1/tickets", headers: auth_headers("acme", new_owner_token)
    assert_response :forbidden

    Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme").update!(cancelled_at: 91.days.ago)
    assert_equal 1, Account.purge_expired!
    assert_nil Ticket.find_by(id: avery_ticket_id)
    assert_equal avery["id"] * 0, Comment.where(ticket_id: avery_ticket_id).count
  end

  test "pagination and ordering for requests, tickets, and comments" do
    create_and_verify_account(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test")
    create_and_verify_customer(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test")
    avery_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password").dig("session", "token")
    owner_token = sign_in(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password").dig("session", "token")

    ticket_ids = []
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-01 10:00:00 UTC") do
      5.times do |i|
        travel 1.minute
        post "/api/v1/requests",
             params: { request: { subject: "Issue #{i + 1}", comment: { body: "Initial #{i + 1}" } } },
             headers: auth_headers("acme", avery_token),
             as: :json
        assert_response :created
        ticket_ids << json_response.dig("request", "id")
      end

      # Reply to the oldest ticket (Issue 1) so it becomes the most recently active
      travel 5.minutes
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ticket_ids[0]}",
            params: { ticket: { comment: { body: "Staff reply" } } },
            headers: auth_headers("acme", owner_token),
            as: :json
      assert_response :success

      # Add more comments to Issue 1 to test oldest-first ordering and pagination
      travel 1.minute
      patch "/api/v1/requests/#{ticket_ids[0]}",
            params: { request: { comment: { body: "Customer follow-up" } } },
            headers: auth_headers("acme", avery_token),
            as: :json
      assert_response :success
    end

    # Page 1 of requests (per_page=2): recently active first -> [Issue 1, Issue 5]
    get "/api/v1/requests?page=1&per_page=2", headers: auth_headers("acme", avery_token)
    assert_response :success
    assert_equal 5, json_response["count"]
    assert_equal 1, json_response["page"]
    assert_equal 2, json_response["per_page"]
    assert_equal 2, json_response["next_page"]

    # Page 2 of tickets (per_page=2): [Issue 4, Issue 3]

The heart of the matter: incoming emails need to generate tickets. Crucially, I need to handle blank or missing subjects gracefully. If the subject is missing, the ticket must still be created, and the blank subject should not result in a validation error causing the entire delivery to fail. I need to handle multipart emails (text/plain + text/html or HTML-only or single-part text/plain). I need to ensure the ticket opens properly (status "open", subject, customer, account) and an initial comment. I also need to make sure that only *email-origin* tickets trigger staff replies to requesters. The existing tests should not expect delivery of an email when a ticket is opened via API.

Business identification is critical. I've got to extract the business from the recipients (To, Cc), *ignoring* mail addressed to multiple businesses. Addresses in the support domain are matched to `Account` instances. This means I have to handle cases where there are multiple support domains or canceled accounts. In particular, I must account for where the "To" address has the support domain, but the "Cc" does not. I need to make sure I deduplicate recipients (and, if the recipient is included in both "To" and "Cc", that this counts as only one business). I also need to ensure that sub-addressing is properly handled when identifying the correct business.

Reuse existing customers! If a user already exists, use them. If they don't, create them. A customer without an account portal password is created, I need to generate a secure random password and store it. When creating a customer from email, extract the name from the "From" header (display name first, then local part, and lastly, the email address). I must *not* verify the account upon email receipt. Furthermore, I must not create a duplicate user when a staff member emails support, and if a customer is suspended or pending verification.

The key interaction is between staff replies and customer replies. Public replies from staff on *email-origin* tickets need an email to the requester. Each ticket must have a private reply address with an unguessable token or secret key, such as `acme+<token>@support.example.test`, NOT just `acme@support.example.test`. The private address ensures that *only* the requester can reply to that ticket, regardless of their email, not just anybody. So, if a staff member posts a reply, the email should have the requester's email and a `Reply-To` (and possibly `From`) set to this private address.

When a staff member replies to the customer, I have to set up both the `to` and `reply_to` headers. I need to set the `reply_to` to the private address (e.g., `acme+<token>@support.example.test`) and choose whether `from` is the plain support domain, or the private address. A customer hitting "Reply" in their mail client will reply to the `Reply-To` address (or, if there is no `Reply-To`, to the `From` address).

require "mail"

module ActionMailbox
  # The +InboundEmail+ is an Active Record that keeps a reference to the raw email stored in Active Storage
  # and tracks the status of processing. By default, incoming emails will go through the following lifecycle:
  #
  # * Pending: Just received by one of the ingress controllers and scheduled for routing.
  # * Processing: During active processing, while a specific mailbox is running its #process method.
  # * Delivered: Successfully processed by the specific mailbox.
  # * Failed: An exception was raised during the specific mailbox's execution of the +#process+ method.
  # * Bounced: Rejected processing by the specific mailbox and bounced to sender.
  #
  # Once the +InboundEmail+ has reached the status of being either +delivered+, +failed+, or +bounced+,
  # it'll count as having been +#processed?+. Once processed, the +InboundEmail+ will be scheduled for
  # automatic incineration at a later point.
  #
  # When working with an +InboundEmail+, you'll usually interact with the parsed version of the source,
  # which is available as a +Mail+ object from +#mail+. But you can also access the raw source directly
  # using the +#source+ method.
  #
  # Examples:
  #
  #   inbound_email.mail.from # => 'david@loudthinking.com'
  #   inbound_email.source # Returns the full rfc822 source of the email as text
  class InboundEmail < Record
    include Incineratable, MessageId, Routable

    has_one_attached :raw_email, service: ActionMailbox.storage_service
    enum :status, %i[ pending processing delivered failed bounced ]

    def mail
      @mail ||= Mail.from_source(source)
    end

    def source
      @source ||= raw_email.download
    end

    def processed?
      delivered? || failed? || bounced?
    end

    def instrumentation_payload # :nodoc:
      {
        id: id,
        message_id: message_id,
        status: status
      }
    end
  end
end

# The +Message-ID+ as specified by rfc822 is supposed to be a unique identifier for that individual email.
# That makes it an ideal tracking token for debugging and forensics, just like +X-Request-Id+ does for
# web request.
#
# If an inbound email does not, against the rfc822 mandate, specify a Message-ID, one will be generated
# using the approach from +Mail::MessageIdField+.
module ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::MessageId
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    # Create a new +InboundEmail+ from the raw +source+ of the email, which is uploaded as an Active Storage
    # attachment called +raw_email+. Before the upload, extract the Message-ID from the +source+ and set
    # it as an attribute on the new +InboundEmail+.
    def create_and_extract_message_id!(source, **options)
      message_checksum = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(source)
      message_id = extract_message_id(source) || generate_missing_message_id(message_checksum)

      create! raw_email: create_and_upload_raw_email!(source),
        message_id: message_id, message_checksum: message_checksum, **options
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      nil
    end

        Mail.from_source(source).message_id rescue nil
      end

        Mail::MessageIdField.new("<#{message_checksum}@#{::Socket.gethostname}.mail>").message_id.tap do |message_id|

        end
      end

                                               service_name: ActionMailbox.storage_service
      end
  end

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into Action Mailbox's Deduplication Strategy**

Okay, hold on a second! I'm really digging into the Action Mailbox source code and something critical just jumped out at me in the `action_mailbox_inbound_emails` schema: that uniqueness index on `[message_id, message_checksum]`! That's the key.

So, first thing I'm thinking: if we get the same email, same `Message-ID`, but with a slightly different raw source (maybe a different relay hop added a `Received` header, or a whitespace change), Action Mailbox *won't* de-duplicate by `Message-ID` alone, because of that `message_checksum` in the index. That's fine, it makes sense. Different content, different checksum.

But then, this sentence… "Deduplicate deliveries by Message-ID. Invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry." This has serious implications. Let's break this down further.

What even *defines* an "invalid delivery"? Okay, let's list all the cases:

*   Unauthenticated relay request (401) or unsupported media type (415) - these never even create an `InboundEmail`. Got it.
*   The email is empty or unparseable, or missing `From`, `Subject`, or `Body`. Validation errors in the ticket/comment process. Transient exceptions.
*   Now, here's where it gets interesting. Say we get an email with `Message-ID: <abc@example.com>` that's initially invalid for some reason (maybe it's missing a subject or body, has a processing error, or an invalid sender), and it *fails* to create a ticket or comment. If we had a table or flag that said, "seen that Message-ID before," before the processing was actually *successful*, it could block a valid retry later on!

Let's assume that we've recorded that the `<abc@example.com>` email *failed* and has a `status: failed`. We don't want the system to block a *valid* retry of the email! What if that later retry has the same *or* a different `message_checksum` but still the same `message_id`?

Okay, so I see now. If the `InboundEmail` is `failed`, what happens in `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.create_and_extract_message_id!`? Looking at the code, it uses `.create!`. If `[message_id, message_checksum]` already exists, `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` is raised, and the method returns `nil`. No routing!

Now, the main concern I have is how to handle a valid retry, with the same `Message-ID`. If we checked a table for *all* seen `Message-ID`s, even failed/invalid ones, that retry would be blocked as a duplicate. And, if the exact same content fails, retrying the exact same bytes would *still* be invalid.

class FrontendCorsMiddleware
  ALLOWED_METHODS = "GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, HEAD".freeze
  ALLOWED_HEADERS = "Authorization, Content-Type, X-Helpdesk-Account, Accept, Origin, X-Requested-With".freeze

  def initialize(app)
    @app = app
  end

  def call(env)
    request_origin = env["HTTP_ORIGIN"]
    origin_allowed = origin_allowed?(request_origin)

    if env["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "OPTIONS" && request_origin.present?
      headers = { "Vary" => "Origin" }
      headers.merge!(cors_headers(request_origin)) if origin_allowed
      return [ 204, headers, [] ]
    end

    status, headers, body = @app.call(env)
    headers = headers.dup

    if request_origin.present?
      append_vary_origin(headers)
      headers.merge!(cors_headers(request_origin)) if origin_allowed
    end

    [ status, headers, body ]
  end

  private

  def origin_allowed?(request_origin)
    return false if request_origin.blank?

    configured = normalize_origin(ENV.fetch("HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL", "http://localhost:3001"))
    incoming = normalize_origin(request_origin)
    configured.present? && incoming == configured

    uri = URI.parse(url.to_s.strip)

    default_port = (scheme == "https" ? 443 : 80)

    port && port != default_port ? "#{scheme}://#{host}:#{port}" : "#{scheme}://#{host}"

**Deep Dive into Email Support Design**

Okay, first things first, that `FrontendCorsMiddleware` isn't going to mess with the `/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` route, so that's one less thing to worry about. Now, let's really nail down the details and think through every single edge case.

### Support Domain and Addresses

First, the support domain. We're going to grab it dynamically from the `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN` environment variable. It's important that it's read dynamically, not cached, so changes to the environment take effect immediately. We'll use a helper method, maybe in a `SupportEmail` module or on the `Account` or `Ticket` models, like `SupportEmail.support_domain`.

Okay, the plain support address for an account is straightforward:  `"#{account.subdomain}@#{SupportEmail.support_domain}"`.  But the private reply address for a ticket... that's where things get interesting.  Do *all* tickets need a reply token, or just email-origin ones?  Do we need to track the "origin" of the ticket to determine this?  Let's keep an eye on that.

The key is, "Give each ticket a private reply address at the support domain, so the customer's next email returns to the right conversation."

If we create a `reply_token` (e.g., using `SecureRandom.hex(16)` and a unique index on the DB column) on ticket creation, and track where the ticket came from, then we'll need to figure out the right format.  It's between `#{account.subdomain}+#{reply_token}@#{SupportEmail.support_domain}` and `reply+#{reply_token}@#{SupportEmail.support_domain}`.

Let's break down the logic of both.

If the format is `#{account.subdomain}+#{reply_token}@#{SupportEmail.support_domain}`, it means we're using subaddressing with the plus sign, which is completely RFC-valid.

*   If the recipient is `acme@support.example.test` (the plain support address), it targets the business `acme` directly.
*   If the recipient is `acme+<token>@support.example.test`, it targets the business `acme` AND the specific reply token.
*   If an email goes to *multiple* businesses at the support domain, we ignore it.
*   If an email goes to `acme+<token>` and `acme@`, it's still the same business. The reply address identifies the ticket, so it should route as expected.
*   We can avoid collisions with business subdomains (like a "reply" subdomain) by using `<subdomain>+<token>`.
*   And yes, `+` subaddressing is completely RFC 5322/6531 valid. Ruby's `Mail` gem, `URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP`, and standard MTAs should support it.  We need to confirm the parsing.
*   We've got to double-check that `Mail::Address` parses the `+` just fine. `Mail::Address.new("acme+abc123@support.example.test").local` should give us `"acme+abc123"`. The domain should be `"support.example.test"`.
*   We also need to consider case-sensitivity. Since email local parts are case-insensitive, we'll downcase everything. The `reply_token` will be lowercase hex anyway, so we're good there. Using `SecureRandom.hex(16)` provides 128 bits of entropy! We are good!

Finally, let's make sure `ticket.as_ticket_json` or `ticket.as_request_json` doesn't need to change to support this new reply-to structure. It's important to look at the existing tests to make sure that they aren't asserting on keys in these methods.

require "test_helper"

class UsersSuspensionAndAssignmentTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)
    { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain, "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}" }
  end

  def create_verified_customer(subdomain:, name:, email:, password: "my-customer-password")
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
         params: { user: { name: name, email: email, password: password } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    token = extract_token_from_email(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/verify-email")[:token]

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
         params: { email_verification: { token: token } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
         as: :json
    assert_response :success
    json_response["user"]
  end

  def invite_and_accept(subdomain:, admin_token:, email:, role:, name:, password: "team-password")
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
         params: { invitation: { email: email, role: role } },
         headers: auth_headers(subdomain, admin_token),
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    token = extract_token_from_email(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/accept-invitation")[:token]

    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
         params: { invitation_acceptance: { token: token, name: name, password: password } },
         headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
         as: :json
    assert_response :created
    json_response["user"]

**Deep Dive into Action Mailbox and Email Handling**

Okay, so I've been digging into how Action Mailbox handles email, and some interesting nuances are surfacing. First, I noticed that `Mail` gem's handling of the `Message-ID` header has some quirks. Specifically:

1.  A standard `Message-ID` format, like `"Message-ID: <abc@example.com>"` correctly extracts `"abc@example.com"`.
2.  Even without the angle brackets, `"Message-ID: abc@example.com"` is still extracted as `"abc@example.com"`.
3.  Critically, `"Message-ID: <>"` is treated as `"<>"` and not `nil`! This could be a problem in checks where we expect `nil`. We might need to consider `"<>"` as a special case.
4.  And *here's* the kicker: a blank `"Message-ID:"` header actually causes `Mail.new` to generate a random message ID! This is problematic because `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::MessageId#extract_message_id` uses `Mail.from_source(source).message_id`. This means that if retries are involved and the header is blank, we'll get a *different* random ID on each retry, unless a checksum is used.

I also observed that even seemingly simple, invalid "From" addresses, like `"From: bad-email"`, are parsed, with the bad address extracted into a list, meaning there is no validation at this stage.

Then I started thinking about `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail` and retries, and what happens when we're creating ActiveStorage blobs and a `RecordNotUnique` exception happens. The `create_and_extract_message_id!` method is where this gets tricky.

Specifically, I'm concerned about the sequence of events with `create_and_upload_raw_email!` happening *before* the `create!` call, and the potential for `RecordNotUnique` on retries. I'm imagining a situation where the blob is created, and *then* the `create!` fails, leaving us in a somewhat inconsistent state.

But now, I'm thinking I can enhance the retry behavior cleanly by prepending a module, `InboundEmailRetryable`, into `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail`. This module checks if an `InboundEmail` with the same `message_id` and `message_checksum` already exists.

*   If the record doesn't exist, we proceed with the normal behavior.
*   If the record *does* exist AND is `delivered?`, `pending?`, or `processing?`, we simply return `nil`. We don't need to re-upload the blob.
*   But if the existing record is `failed?` or `bounced?`, we *destroy* the invalid record (and its attached blob) and then retry the `create!` operation. This is really clean! We're essentially cleaning up a failed attempt and allowing a fresh try.

require "cgi"

class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  AUTO_PRECEDENCE_VALUES = %w[bulk list junk auto_reply auto-reply].freeze
  LIST_HEADERS = %w[
    list-id
    list-unsubscribe
    list-post
    list-owner
    list-subscribe
    list-help
    list-archive
    mailing-list
    x-mailing-list
    x-list-id
  ].freeze

  SupportTarget = Struct.new(:subdomain, :reply_token, :invalid_plus, keyword_init: true)

  def process
    return if already_processed?

    if automated_or_list_mail?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    targets = extract_support_targets
    subdomains = targets.map(&:subdomain).reject(&:blank?).uniq
    if subdomains.size != 1
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if targets.any?(&:invalid_plus)
      bounced!
      return
    end

    account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomains.first)
    if account.nil? || account.cancelled?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    reply_tokens = targets.filter_map(&:reply_token).uniq
    if reply_tokens.size > 1
      bounced!
      return
    end

    from_addr = safe_from_address
    sender_email = from_addr&.address.to_s.strip.downcase
    unless sender_email.match?(URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP)
      bounced!
      return
    end

    body = extract_plain_text_body
    if body.blank?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if reply_tokens.size == 1
      process_reply(
        account: account,
        reply_token: reply_tokens.first,
        sender_email: sender_email,
        body: body
      )
    else
      process_new_ticket(
        account: account,
        sender_email: sender_email,
        sender_name: derive_sender_name(from_addr, sender_email),
        body: body
      )
    end
  end

  private

  def already_processed?
    InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
  end

  def automated_or_list_mail?
    auto_submitted = header_values("auto-submitted").map(&:downcase)
    return true if auto_submitted.any? { |v| v.present? && v != "no" }

    precedences = (header_values("precedence") + header_values("x-precedence")).map(&:downcase)
    return true if (precedences & AUTO_PRECEDENCE_VALUES).any?

    return true if LIST_HEADERS.any? { |name| header_values(name).any?(&:present?) }

    return true if header_values("x-auto-response-suppress").any?(&:present?)
    return true if header_values("x-autoreply").any? { |v| v.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(v.downcase) }
    return true if header_values("x-autorespond").any? { |v| v.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(v.downcase) }

    if !mail.header[:return_path].nil?
      rp_values = header_values("return-path")
      return true if rp_values.all? { |v| v.blank? || v == "<>" }
    end

    return true if mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase == "multipart/report"

    sender_local = safe_from_address&.local.to_s.strip.downcase
    return true if sender_local == "mailer-daemon"

    false
  end

  def header_values(name)
    raw = mail.header[name]
    return [] if raw.nil?

    fields = raw.is_a?(Array) ? raw : [ raw ]
    fields.map { |f| f.value.to_s.strip }
  rescue StandardError
    []
  end

  def extract_support_targets
    support_domain = SupportEmail.support_domain
    addresses = safe_recipient_addresses

    addresses.filter_map do |addr|
      domain = addr.domain.to_s.strip.downcase
      next unless domain == support_domain

      local = addr.local.to_s.strip.downcase
      if local.include?("+")
        subdomain, reply_token = local.split("+", 2)
        SupportTarget.new(
          subdomain: subdomain,
          reply_token: reply_token.presence,
          invalid_plus: subdomain.blank? || reply_token.blank?
        )
      else
        SupportTarget.new(
          subdomain: local,
          reply_token: nil,
          invalid_plus: false
        )
      end
    end
  end

  def safe_recipient_addresses
    addresses = []
    %i[to_addresses cc_addresses bcc_addresses x_original_to_addresses x_forwarded_to_addresses].each do |method_name|
      begin
        addresses.concat(Array(mail.public_send(method_name)))
      rescue StandardError
        # Ignore malformed individual recipient header
      end
    end
    addresses
  end

  def safe_from_address
    mail.from_address
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def derive_sender_name(from_addr, sender_email)
    display_name = decode_to_utf8(from_addr.display_name.to_s).strip
    return display_name if display_name.present?

    local_part = from_addr.local.to_s.strip
    local_part.present? ? local_part : sender_email
  end

  def extract_plain_text_body
    raw = if mail.text_part
            decode_to_utf8(mail.text_part.decoded, mail.text_part.charset)
          elsif !mail.multipart?
            mime = mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase
            if mime.blank? || mime == "text/plain"
              decode_to_utf8(mail.decoded, mail.charset)
            elsif mime == "text/html"
              html_to_text(decode_to_utf8(mail.decoded, mail.charset))
            end
          elsif mail.html_part
            html_to_text(decode_to_utf8(mail.html_part.decoded, mail.html_part.charset))
          end

    raw.to_s.gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
  rescue StandardError
    ""
  end

  def html_to_text(html)
    with_breaks = html.to_s
                      .gsub(/<\s*br\s*\/?>/i, "\n")
                      .gsub(/<\/\s*(?:p|div|li|tr|h[1-6]|blockquote)\s*>/i, "\n")
    sanitized = ActionView::Base.full_sanitizer.sanitize(with_breaks)
    CGI.unescapeHTML(sanitized)
  end

  def decode_to_utf8(value, charset = nil)
    str = value.to_s.dup
    if charset.present? && str.encoding == Encoding::ASCII_8BIT
      encoding = Encoding.find(charset) rescue Encoding::UTF_8
      str.force_encoding(encoding)
    end
    str.encode("UTF-8", invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: "")
  rescue StandardError
    value.to_s.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub("")
  end

  def process_reply(account:, reply_token:, sender_email:, body:)
    ticket = account.tickets.find_by(reply_token: reply_token)
    if ticket.nil?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    requester = ticket.requester
    if requester.email != sender_email || requester.suspended?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      InboundEmailReceipt.create!(message_id: inbound_email.message_id, ticket: ticket)

      ticket.comments.create!(
        author: requester,
        body: body,
        public: true
      )

      if ticket.status.in?(%w[pending solved])
        ticket.update!(status: "open")
      end
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # Duplicate delivery by Message-ID; ignore cleanly
    nil
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    bounced!
  end

  def process_new_ticket(account:, sender_email:, sender_name:, body:)
    subject = decode_to_utf8(mail.subject.to_s).strip
    if subject.blank?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    raw_verification_token = nil
    created_user = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      receipt = InboundEmailReceipt.create!(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)

      user = account.users.find_by(email: sender_email)
      if user
        if user.suspended?
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end
      else
        user = account.users.build(
          role: "customer",
          name: sender_name,
          email: sender_email,
          password: SecureRandom.base58(24)
        )
        user.save!
        raw_verification_token = user.generate_email_verification_token!
        created_user = user
      end

      ticket = account.tickets.create!(
        requester: user,
        subject: subject,
        status: "open",
        origin: "email"
      )

      ticket.comments.create!(
        author: user,
        body: body,
        public: true
      )

      receipt.update!(ticket: ticket)
    end

    if created_user.nil? && account.users.find_by(email: sender_email)&.suspended?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if created_user && raw_verification_token.present?
      UserMailer.email_verification(created_user, raw_verification_token).deliver_now
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # Duplicate delivery by Message-ID; ignore cleanly
    nil
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    bounced!
  end
end

**Refining the Ticket Creation Process for Robustness**

Okay, let's break down this ticket creation flow and tighten it up, especially regarding user suspension and potential race conditions. First, I need to focus on how we handle suspended users. Right now, in `process_new_ticket`, when we check if a user is suspended, we can either: do a query and check *before* the transaction, or check inside the transaction. I think the latter is cleaner – we can set a boolean flag, `suspended_sender`, and raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback` within the transaction if the user is suspended. Then, outside the transaction, we can easily check the flag and call `bounced!`. This avoids a second database query *after* the transaction, making it more efficient and readable.

Next, I need to consider `InboundEmailReceipt.create!`. If this raises `RecordNotUnique`, say, due to a duplicate message ID, PostgreSQL will abort the *entire* transaction, and we can catch that outside the transaction's block, which is perfect and clean. However, the same logic will not hold true in the case of `account.users.build(...)` hitting `RecordNotUnique` due to a race condition. It's a different animal. This is where I've got to be extra careful. If we have two emails from a brand-new customer with the same email (but different message IDs), we'll hit that unique index on `(account_id, email)` on the `users` table. Rescuing `RecordNotUnique` *outside* the transaction would actually swallow the user email collision. Instead, I need to distinguish between `InboundEmailReceipt` and `User` uniqueness. I can do that by either checking if the receipt exists inside the transaction *before* attempting the `create!`, or use a separate rescue block specifically for `InboundEmailReceipt.create!`.

I need to be aware of how PostgreSQL handles `RecordNotUnique` within transactions. If it happens, you either have to use a `requires_new: true` (savepoint) or make sure that you insert the `InboundEmailReceipt` as the *first* statement within the transaction, or specifically check the `message_id` within the rescue block.

And finally, if `user.save!` hits `RecordNotUnique` due to a concurrent signup, that's fine; we can retry that or just look for the existing user.

  end

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !cancelled?
  end

  def reactivable?
    cancelled? && cancelled_at >= CANCELLATION_RETENTION_PERIOD.ago
  end

  def cancellation_expired?
    cancelled? && cancelled_at < CANCELLATION_RETENTION_PERIOD.ago
  end

  def cancel!
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: Time.current)
      Session.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  def as_portal_json
    {
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain
    }
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      owner_id: owner_id,
      cancelled: cancelled?,
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def clear_owner_reference
    update_columns(owner_id: nil) if owner_id.present?
  end
end

require "securerandom"

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  ORIGINS = %w[portal email].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :inbound_email_receipts, dependent: :nullify

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(s) { s.to_s.strip }

  before_validation :ensure_reply_token, on: :create

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validates :origin, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ORIGINS }
  validates :reply_token, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account

  scope :recently_active_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :matching_query, ->(query) {
    term = query.to_s.strip
    return all if term.blank?

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(term)}%"
    where(
      "tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern OR EXISTS (" \
      "SELECT 1 FROM comments " \
      "WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id " \
      "AND comments.public = TRUE " \
      "AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern" \
      ")",
      pattern: pattern
    )
  }

  def email_origin?
    origin == "email"
  end

  def reply_address
    SupportEmail.reply_address_for_ticket(self)
  end

  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  def as_ticket_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      priority: priority,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      requester: {
        id: requester.id,
        name: requester.name,
        email: requester.email
      },
      assignee_id: assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee ? {
        id: assignee.id,
        name: assignee.name
      } : nil,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def ensure_reply_token
    self.reply_token = SecureRandom.hex(16) if reply_token.blank?
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return if requester.nil? || account.nil?
    return if requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
  end

  def assignee_must_be_active_staff_in_account
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    if assignee.nil? || assignee.account_id != account_id || !assignee.staff? || assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class TicketsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_account!
      before_action :require_session!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :require_staff!

      def index
        scope = current_account.tickets.includes(:requester, :assignee).recently_active_first

        if params[:status].present?
          status_filter = params[:status].to_s
          unless Ticket::STATUSES.include?(status_filter)
            return render json: { error: "Invalid status filter" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
          scope = scope.where(status: status_filter)
        end

        if params[:priority].present?
          priority_filter = params[:priority].to_s
          unless Ticket::PRIORITIES.include?(priority_filter)
            return render json: { error: "Invalid priority filter" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
          scope = scope.where(priority: priority_filter)
        end

        if params[:assignee_id].present?
          assignee_filter = params[:assignee_id].to_s
          if assignee_filter == "unassigned"
            scope = scope.where(assignee_id: nil)
          else
            assignee_id = parse_filter_id(assignee_filter)
            if assignee_id.nil?
              return render json: { error: "Invalid assignee_id filter" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
            end
            scope = scope.where(assignee_id: assignee_id)
          end
        end

        if params[:requester_id].present?
          requester_id = parse_filter_id(params[:requester_id].to_s)
          if requester_id.nil?
            return render json: { error: "Invalid requester_id filter" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
          end
          scope = scope.where(requester_id: requester_id)
        end

        if params[:q].present?
          scope = scope.matching_query(params[:q])
        end

        result = paginate(scope)

        render json: result[:meta].merge(
          tickets: result[:records].map(&:as_ticket_json)
        ), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        ticket = current_account.tickets.includes(:requester, :assignee).find(params[:id])
        render json: { ticket: ticket.as_ticket_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def update
        ticket = current_account.tickets.find(params[:id])
        ticket_attrs = params.require(:ticket)
        unless ticket_attrs.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          return render json: { error: "Invalid ticket payload" }, status: :bad_request
        end

        permitted = ticket_attrs.permit(:status, :assignee_id, :priority, comment: [ :body, :public ])

        has_comment = ticket_attrs.key?(:comment)
        has_status = permitted.key?(:status) && !permitted[:status].nil?
        has_assignee_id = permitted.key?(:assignee_id)
        has_priority = permitted.key?(:priority) && !permitted[:priority].nil?

        unless has_comment || has_status || has_assignee_id || has_priority
          return render json: { error: "Comment, status, priority, or assignee is required" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        if has_comment && !ticket_attrs[:comment].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          return render json: { error: "Comment must be an object" }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end

        comment_attrs = has_comment ? (permitted[:comment] || {}) : {}
        raw_public = comment_attrs.key?(:public) && !comment_attrs[:public].nil? ? comment_attrs[:public] : true
        is_public = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(raw_public)
        is_public = true if is_public.nil?

        created_comment = nil
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          status_changed = has_status && permitted[:status].to_s != ticket.status
          should_bump_timestamps = status_changed || (has_comment && is_public)

          ticket.assign_attributes(status: permitted[:status]) if has_status
          ticket.assign_attributes(assignee_id: permitted[:assignee_id]) if has_assignee_id
          ticket.assign_attributes(priority: permitted[:priority]) if has_priority

          if ticket.changed? || !ticket.valid?
            ticket.record_timestamps = false unless should_bump_timestamps
            ticket.save!
          end

          if has_comment
            created_comment = ticket.comments.create!(
              author: current_user,
              body: comment_attrs[:body],
              public: is_public
            )
          end
        end

        if created_comment&.public? && ticket.email_origin?
          TicketMailer.staff_reply(ticket, created_comment).deliver_now
        end

        render json: { ticket: ticket.reload.as_ticket_json }, status: :ok
      ensure
        ticket&.record_timestamps = true
      end

      def comments
        ticket = current_account.tickets.find(params[:id])
        scope = ticket.comments.includes(:author).oldest_first
        result = paginate(scope)

        render json: result[:meta].merge(
          comments: result[:records].map(&:as_api_json)
        ), status: :ok
      end

      private

      def parse_filter_id(raw)
        return nil unless raw.match?(/\A\d+\z/)

        parsed = raw.to_i
        parsed >= 1 ? parsed : nil
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "cgi"

class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  AUTO_PRECEDENCE_VALUES = %w[bulk list junk auto_reply auto-reply].freeze
  LIST_HEADERS = %w[
    list-id
    list-unsubscribe
    list-post
    list-owner
    list-subscribe
    list-help
    list-archive
    mailing-list
    x-mailing-list
    x-list-id
  ].freeze

  SupportTarget = Struct.new(:subdomain, :reply_token, :invalid_plus, keyword_init: true)

  def process
    return if already_processed?

    if automated_or_list_mail?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    targets = extract_support_targets
    subdomains = targets.map(&:subdomain).reject(&:blank?).uniq
    if subdomains.size != 1
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if targets.any?(&:invalid_plus)
      bounced!
      return
    end

    account = Account.find_by(subdomain: subdomains.first)
    if account.nil? || account.cancelled?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    reply_tokens = targets.filter_map(&:reply_token).uniq
    if reply_tokens.size > 1
      bounced!
      return
    end

    from_addr = safe_from_address
    sender_email = from_addr&.address.to_s.strip.downcase
    unless sender_email.match?(URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP)
      bounced!
      return
    end

    body = extract_plain_text_body
    if body.blank?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if reply_tokens.size == 1
      process_reply(
        account: account,
        reply_token: reply_tokens.first,
        sender_email: sender_email,
        body: body
      )
    else
      process_new_ticket(
        account: account,
        sender_email: sender_email,
        sender_name: derive_sender_name(from_addr, sender_email),
        body: body
      )
    end
  end

  private

  def already_processed?
    InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
  end

  def automated_or_list_mail?
    auto_submitted = header_values("auto-submitted").map(&:downcase)
    return true if auto_submitted.any? { |v| v.present? && v != "no" }

    precedences = (header_values("precedence") + header_values("x-precedence")).map(&:downcase)
    return true if (precedences & AUTO_PRECEDENCE_VALUES).any?

    return true if LIST_HEADERS.any? { |name| header_values(name).any?(&:present?) }

    return true if header_values("x-auto-response-suppress").any?(&:present?)
    return true if header_values("x-autoreply").any? { |v| v.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(v.downcase) }
    return true if header_values("x-autorespond").any? { |v| v.present? && !%w[no false 0].include?(v.downcase) }

    if !mail.header[:return_path].nil?
      rp_values = header_values("return-path")
      return true if rp_values.all? { |v| v.blank? || v == "<>" }
    end

    return true if mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase == "multipart/report"

    sender_local = safe_from_address&.local.to_s.strip.downcase
    return true if sender_local == "mailer-daemon"

    false
  end

  def header_values(name)
    raw = mail.header[name]
    return [] if raw.nil?

    fields = raw.is_a?(Array) ? raw : [ raw ]
    fields.map { |f| f.value.to_s.strip }
  rescue StandardError
    []
  end

  def extract_support_targets
    support_domain = SupportEmail.support_domain
    addresses = safe_recipient_addresses

    addresses.filter_map do |addr|
      domain = addr.domain.to_s.strip.downcase
      next unless domain == support_domain

      local = addr.local.to_s.strip.downcase
      if local.include?("+")
        subdomain, reply_token = local.split("+", 2)
        SupportTarget.new(
          subdomain: subdomain,
          reply_token: reply_token.presence,
          invalid_plus: subdomain.blank? || reply_token.blank?
        )
      else
        SupportTarget.new(
          subdomain: local,
          reply_token: nil,
          invalid_plus: false
        )
      end
    end
  end

  def safe_recipient_addresses
    addresses = []
    %i[to_addresses cc_addresses bcc_addresses x_original_to_addresses x_forwarded_to_addresses].each do |method_name|
      begin
        addresses.concat(Array(mail.public_send(method_name)))
      rescue StandardError
        # Ignore malformed individual recipient header
      end
    end
    addresses
  end

  def safe_from_address
    mail.from_address
  rescue StandardError
    nil
  end

  def derive_sender_name(from_addr, sender_email)
    display_name = decode_to_utf8(from_addr.display_name.to_s).strip
    return display_name if display_name.present?

    local_part = from_addr.local.to_s.strip
    local_part.present? ? local_part : sender_email
  end

  def extract_plain_text_body
    raw = if mail.text_part
            decode_to_utf8(mail.text_part.decoded, mail.text_part.charset)
          elsif !mail.multipart?
            mime = mail.mime_type.to_s.downcase
            if mime.blank? || mime == "text/plain"
              decode_to_utf8(mail.decoded, mail.charset)
            elsif mime == "text/html"
              html_to_text(decode_to_utf8(mail.decoded, mail.charset))
            end
          elsif mail.html_part
            html_to_text(decode_to_utf8(mail.html_part.decoded, mail.html_part.charset))
          end

    raw.to_s.gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
  rescue StandardError
    ""
  end

  def html_to_text(html)
    with_breaks = html.to_s
                      .gsub(/<\s*br\s*\/?>/i, "\n")
                      .gsub(/<\/\s*(?:p|div|li|tr|h[1-6]|blockquote)\s*>/i, "\n")
    sanitized = ActionView::Base.full_sanitizer.sanitize(with_breaks)
    CGI.unescapeHTML(sanitized)
  end

  def decode_to_utf8(value, charset = nil)
    str = value.to_s.dup
    if charset.present? && str.encoding == Encoding::ASCII_8BIT
      encoding = Encoding.find(charset) rescue Encoding::UTF_8
      str.force_encoding(encoding)
    end
    str.encode("UTF-8", invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: "")
  rescue StandardError
    value.to_s.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8").scrub("")
  end

  def process_reply(account:, reply_token:, sender_email:, body:)
    ticket = account.tickets.find_by(reply_token: reply_token)
    if ticket.nil?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    requester = ticket.requester
    if requester.email != sender_email || requester.suspended?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      InboundEmailReceipt.create!(message_id: inbound_email.message_id, ticket: ticket)

      ticket.comments.create!(
        author: requester,
        body: body,
        public: true
      )

      if ticket.status.in?(%w[pending solved])
        ticket.update!(status: "open")
      end
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique => e
    raise unless e.message.include?("inbound_email_receipts") || InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)

    nil
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    bounced!
  end

  def process_new_ticket(account:, sender_email:, sender_name:, body:)
    subject = decode_to_utf8(mail.subject.to_s).strip
    if subject.blank?
      bounced!
      return
    end

    raw_verification_token = nil
    created_user = nil
    suspended_sender = false

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      receipt = InboundEmailReceipt.create!(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)

      user = account.users.find_by(email: sender_email)
      if user
        if user.suspended?
          suspended_sender = true
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end
      else
        user = account.users.build(
          role: "customer",
          name: sender_name,
          email: sender_email,
          password: SecureRandom.base58(24)
        )
        user.save!
        raw_verification_token = user.generate_email_verification_token!
        created_user = user
      end

      ticket = account.tickets.create!(
        requester: user,
        subject: subject,
        status: "open",
        origin: "email"
      )

      ticket.comments.create!(
        author: user,
        body: body,
        public: true
      )

      receipt.update!(ticket: ticket)
    end

    if suspended_sender
      bounced!
      return
    end

    if created_user && raw_verification_token.present?
      UserMailer.email_verification(created_user, raw_verification_token).deliver_now
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique => e
    raise unless e.message.include?("inbound_email_receipts") || InboundEmailReceipt.exists?(message_id: inbound_email.message_id)

    nil
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    bounced!
  end
end

**Comprehensive Integration Tests for Robust Email Support**

Alright, let's dive in. I need to nail down a truly comprehensive integration test suite for this email support system. I'm thinking about *every* possible scenario, *every* edge case, and all the moving parts. The goal? Rock-solid reliability and bulletproof behavior. Here's how I see it:

First, let's cover the authentication and content type: I'll test for *every* possible failure and success path related to the relay ingress. Missing credentials should trigger a 401 Unauthorized. Wrong password? Same. Incorrect content type (anything besides `application/json`, `text/plain`, or `message/rfc822`)? A clean 415 Unsupported Media Type. A valid request with basic auth and the correct `message/rfc822` content type? That should result in a 204 No Content, with the ticket created *before* the request completes, so we can ensure the ticket is there, right away.

Next, I have to simulate a new customer opening a ticket via email. Plain-text email from a new customer to the support address should: generate an open ticket, the new customer, an unverified customer with the role of "customer." It should also trigger a verification email and test that the user can't log in until they verify. I'll need to explicitly verify the account, then check that they can reset the password and sign in, and finally, view the email-origin request. I should make sure that the system correctly handles emails with and without display names.

Multipart emails? I need to test that the system correctly extracts the plain-text body, even if the email also includes HTML and attachments. Also, I need to verify that we can support a custom support domain, and emails to that domain are correctly routed.

Now, for existing customers. We must ensure that verified customers emailing the support address don't receive unnecessary verification emails. Unverified customers should also be handled correctly; the system should reuse existing customer accounts and *not* send out an additional verification email.

I need to test the logic around finding the correct business from the "To" and "Cc" fields. I want to be sure that the system recognizes the correct support email address to route to, and that emails with multiple support addresses (or unknown addresses) are ignored. Emails to a cancelled account should also be ignored until the account is reactivated, and then they can be retried.

Let's not forget staff replies. A public staff reply to an email-origin ticket *must* send an email to the requester, with the correct reply-to address, and a sensible "Re:" subject. Internal notes or status-only changes should *never* send an email. Similarly, public replies on portal-origin tickets shouldn't trigger an email either.

Then, there's the customer replying via the private reply address. Replies to the ticket's private reply address should reopen the ticket to 'open'. Even after the ticket is marked 'solved', a reply via the private address should reopen the ticket. However, if the customer sends a *new* email to the regular support address, it should create a *new* ticket. Also, I need to test reply-all scenarios, ensuring that they route to the correct existing ticket. Replies that involve multiple businesses should be ignored.

Who can reply? Only the *requester* can reply by email. I need to verify that any email from a different address is rejected. Invalid reply tokens, cross-tenant tokens, must also be ignored and *not* create new tickets or comments.

I need to nail down deduplication and valid retries: Identical messages with the same Message-ID should only create one ticket or comment. Even if there are slight differences in headers, I should ensure the system still deduplicates properly. If an invalid delivery (blank subject, missing From, etc.) occurs, the system should return 204. Crucially, a *valid* retry with the same Message-ID *must* succeed after the initial invalid delivery. The invalid delivery shouldn't block a valid one! This is also true if the account is cancelled and then reactivated.

Finally, let's make sure we ignore automated emails and common list mail headers. I must handle `Auto-Submitted`, `Precedence`, `List-Id`, `List-Unsubscribe`, `X-Auto-Response-Suppress`, `Return-Path`, and `Content-Type: multipart/report` scenarios, as they should be ignored, and not generate unnecessary tickets.

That's the plan. Now, it's time to build the suite.

**A Quick Debug & Clean Fix for a Rails ActiveJob Issue**

Okay, wow, that was a good catch running those tests! This error message – `"NotImplementedError: Use a queueing backend to enqueue jobs in the future"` – that's a classic sign, and I know exactly where to look. It's that `InlineAdapter#enqueue_at` method in Rails 8.1, throwing that exception.

And the culprit? Action Mailbox! Specifically, that `ActionMailbox::InboundEmail::Incineratable` module. It's calling `incinerate_later` after an update, and *that* job – `ActionMailbox::IncinerationJob` – is using `enqueue_at` with a delay (30 days!). Now, because my test environment is configured with `config.active_job.queue_adapter = :inline`, that's where the problem arises: `enqueue_at` isn't supported by the inline adapter. And because `ActionMailbox.incinerate` is `true`, the job is enqueued with the inline adapter and fails.

The fix? Simple and elegant. In `config/environments/test.rb`, I can just set `config.action_mailbox.incinerate = false`. That disables the incineration logic for the test environment, sidestepping the `enqueue_at` call altogether. Actually, on second thought, maybe I should verify the `test.rb` setup to be sure that `:inline` is used *and* that `incinerate = false` – why would anyone schedule a 30-day delay in tests with inline anyway?

But hold on, could this bite me somewhere else? What if someone *else* is using `ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = :inline` in, say, development or production? Rails defaults to `:async` for those environments, which supports `enqueue_at`, so I should be okay there. This issue really only arises in the `test` environment, which is configured for this specific pattern ("In test, process incoming mail before the request completes so a separate worker isn't needed.").

So, setting `config.action_mailbox.incinerate = false` in `config/environments/test.rb` is the cleanest solution for this `NotImplementedError` in my `test` setup. Time to update that configuration and re-run the tests!
